chunks: And Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he used to say:
If a man has a debt and then dies, the debt becomes due.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: Ismāʿīl, the named narrator in the sanad
key_terms.الدَّيْنُ: the debt itself that is now payable
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt or financial liability owed by a person
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; the point at which the ruling takes effect

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's debt when he dies in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning debt at the time of death. It indicates that when a debtor dies, the term of the debt is no longer deferred and the debt immediately becomes due from his estate.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3709 - Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Abdillah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), that he used to say:
"If a man has a debt and then dies, the debt becomes due."
